checks: A nonzero separating direction has a conic representation with at most two listed normals. If zero is on or outside the body, their two closed caps cover the body and have combined area less than its area.

The two triangles based on the radius have total area RW/2, so W≤2k/R. The far-strip cap inclusion follows from |t|≤W and the two opposite projections of size at least κ. The central-strip upper area is (2TW)W.
For n opposite a least-support direction, the missed portion lies in the slab of width ρ, with transverse length at most 2R. Combining εk≤2Rρ and R²≤8Tk/ε yields ρ²≥ε³k/(32T).
The source at 62c2d01f5a0e7e2a §§1–2, 6 has the same planar, closed-cap and prescribed-normal hypotheses.

overlap.comparison: The three-normal sector theorem assumes source interior and gives sector inequalities. It does not give origin-centered inner and outer balls for arbitrary prescribed positive-spanning normals.
One-body normalization after an affine map does not preserve this original source and its prescribed cap directions.

readability: The hypotheses and the proof use the same scope.
review_method: Independent cold read of the exact frozen candidate, followed by source, hypothesis, overlap and arithmetic checks.
summary: The fixed-source separation and two width estimates give all three quantitative bounds with the claimed constants.
